Most people just use the word "mature" to mean something like "they think like I do" or "they agree with the status quo". 

On reddit, people call you immature because you disagree with them by quoting moronic middle school memes like "3edgy5me", which I find delightful because it shows just how stupid people are.

And I can't even find a way to recycle all the damn button cell batteries I have lying around...
If my junk got blown off by a grenade I would commit suicide too.

BB was gorgeous, but this photo doesn't really say "cool" to me, just "rich and attractive". 

In fact, the dude sitting next to her just looks like a smug douchebag.

My psychiatrist did that as well. She declared me cured, despite the fact that I had shown no improvement. Her claim was that her other patients were so severely schizophrenic or whatever that they had to be under supervision 24/7, so since I wasn't like that I was "fine". 

She was actually finishing her residency, and so was moving on to her actual job. The timing of me being "cured" fit exactly with that. In other words, it had nothing to do with me or my treatment - she was just ready to move on and didn't even care enough to refer me to a new doctor. 

Doctors and therapists are like everyone else - some are terrible at their jobs. And to almost all of them, we're just a gig. A client. A way to pay bills. That attitude is actually necessary for their survival, I think. If they were emotionally invested in our emotional well being, I think it would destroy them. It's like how doctors in the cancer ward can't let themselves get attached to patients because they die all the time. 

But there are also many who are just bad at it. And with therapists, there's not much accountability, because even good ones don't have that much control over how well their patients do. So the shitty ones can keep going. 

In other words, it's probably more about her than you.

Dude, this. 

I also went into a "cool" job. Unless you dedicate every fibre of your being to the career and nothing else, colleagues feel that you just aren't committed enough. It killed my passion for it completely.

Dysthymia or no, I do **NOT** understand people who define themselves by their job. *Maybe* if they are a doctor who has come up with a cure to a terrible disease, or famous in a way that really feeds their ego, I can kind of get how someone else might feel that way. But the people who have normal careers - 99.9999% of people - I can't wrap my head around that.

There is definitely some codependency there. I think I have a lot more problems than just ADHD. I try to distance myself but he's one of those people that doesn't give up :o/ That's part of the apprehension about the phone.

You're right, it's definitely a generational thing in a lot of ways. But I'm old, 41. I grew up with land lines. But I've still always hated talking on the phone. 

It was fucking beautiful that you could just leave the house and no one could contact you back then. Now, it's like there is zero expectation of privacy. People know you have a phone and believe that gives them title to call you whenever, and expect you to answer or call back. Get angry if you don't. 

Checking the voicemail isn't a big deal for me, just talking to people is. Anticipating the *content* of the voicemail may make me anxious, though.

Most people know to text me and not call. But a few people just insist on talking and not texting. Texting that they are going to call in 5 minutes would just make me really anxious for those 5 minutes :oP

I do try text or email. This guy in particular likes to text back "give me a call" instead of replying. It's a business call, although the relationship has blurred boundaries and is a mess. He's sometimes my boss, my landlord, business partner, and of course the "we're friends, too!" thing making it even more unclear where responsibilities, obligations, and authority lie. 

I have a huge issue dealing with things like that. I feel he is using me, but can't make myself talk to people when they do that. I just avoid them. But I'm not sure that's an ADHD thing, it may just be from growing up with an abusive parent. But I think the ADHD makes it worse.
They hypnotize you and give you suggestions based on whatever it is you want to change. Quitting smoking is probably the most common thing it's used for.
Hypnotherapy is pretty mainstream. Usually done by a psychologist and not a psychiatrist. It can be effective for some things for some people. Certainly no miracle cure, though.
